1: AN ORDINANCE TO ESTABLISH QUALIFYING DATES AND TIMES FOR THE 1997 GENERAL ELECTION FOR THE OFFICE OF MAYOR OF THE TOWN OF CLERMONT AND TWO COUNCIL POSTS FOR THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF CLERMONT; TO PROVIDE FOR A QUALIFYING FEE; TO PROVIDE FOR ELECTION APPOINTMENTS; TO PROVIDE FOR LOCATIONS AND DEADLINES TO REGISTER TO VOTE IN THE 1997 GENERAL ELECTION; TO PROVIDE FOR SEPARABILITY; AND FOR
2: BE IT ORDAINED BY THE MAYOR AND COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF CLERMONT, GEORGIA THAT THE FOLLOWING QUALIFYING DATES, TIMES AND FEES BE ESTABLISHED FOR THE GENERAL ELECTION TO BE HELD NOVEMBER 4, 1997 FOR THE OFFICE OF MAYOR OF THE TOWN OF CLERMONT, GEORGIA AND TWO COUNCIL POSTS FOR THE TOWN COUNCIL
4:
Each candidate for the office of Mayor of the Town of Clermont, Georgia and each candidate for Council of the Town of Clermont, Georgia will file notice of his candidacy in the office of the Municipal Superintendent of the

municipality. Dates for qualifying are September 8, 9, 10, 11, 1997, during regular office hours; 9:00 A.M. to 5:00 P.M. in the Town Hall of Clermont, Georgia. Notice of the opening and closing dates and the hours for candidates to qualify shall be published at least two weeks prior to the opening of the qualifying period.
5:
(A) The qualifying fee for the office of Mayor of the Town of Clermont, Georgia shall be 3 percent of the annual salary of the Mayor, which will be $27.00 and the qualifying fee for council post shall also be 3 percent of the annual salary of the council post, which will be $21.60.

(B) At least two weeks prior to the opening of qualifications for a special or general municipal election, the governing authority shall publish qualification fees to be paid by candidates seeking election in any such special or general election. Such fee shall be paid to the municipal superintendent at the time a candidate files his notice of candidacy.

(C) A pauper’s affidavit may be filed in lieu of paying the qualifying fee otherwise required by this Ordinance in
6:
instead of paying a qualifying fee shall under oath affirm his poverty and his resulting inability to pay the qualifying fee otherwise required. The form of the affidavit shall be prescribed by the Secretary of State and shall include a financial statement which lists the total

income, assets, liabilities, and other relevant financial information of the candidate and shall indicate on its face that the candidate has neither the assets nor the income to pay the qualifying fee otherwise required. The affidavit shall contain an oath that such candidate has neither the assets nor the income to pay the qualifying fee otherwise required. The following warning shall be printed on the affidavit form prepared by the Secretary of State, to wit: "WARNING; Any person knowingly making any false statement on this affidavit commits the offense of false swearing and shall be guilty of a felony." The election superintendent shall place on the ballot the name of any candidate who subscribes and swears to an oath that such candidate has neither the assets nor the income to pay the qualifying fee otherwise required.
8:
(A) In a general municipal election, no person elected on a write-in vote shall be eligible to hold office unless notice of his intention of candidacy was given 20 or more days prior to the election by the person to be a write-in candidate or by some other person or group of persons qualified to vote in the election, to the Mayor or the Superintendent of the Municipality and by publication in the official gazette of the municipality holding the election.

(B) In addition to the requirements contained in subsection (A), the person or persons giving notice of intention of candidacy for a write-in candidate shall also

file, with the Mayor or Superintendent of the municipality, a copy of the notice as published with an affidavit stating that the notice has been published, with the name of the newspaper and the date of publication, not later than the fifth day after the deadline for filing and publishing such notice. The affidavit may be made by the person giving notice of intention of candidacy or by the publisher of the newspaper in which the notice was published or by an employee of the newspaper designated by the publisher.
9: The Town of Clermont does hereby appoint Ann Culpepper as Election Superintendent, Lawonia Freeman as Municipal Registrar, Lawonia Freeman as Absentee Ballot Clerk and Ann Culpepper as Chief Manager.
10: Anyone wishing to register to vote in the 1997 General Election may do so at the Clermont Town Hall, at the Office of the Hall County Registrar, or as provided by 0.C.G.A. 21- 3-123 until the close of business October 6, 1997.
